items.label: What Is a Dry Freight Trailer?
How to Choose the Right One

props.text: View detailed specifications before you compare trailers.

When it comes to transporting everyday goods, few trailers offer the versatility and dependability of a dry freight trailer. Also known as dry vans, these enclosed box trailers are the backbone of general freight hauling. If you're moving packaged cargo, consumer goods, palletized loads, or non-perishables, dry freight trailers offer the security, efficiency, and flexibility your business needs to keep rolling.

At Sun State Trailers, we work with Florida's owner-operators and fleet managers to match them with the right dry freight trailer for the job, whether they're expanding a fleet or just getting started. Here's what makes these trailers so essential, how to choose the right one, and how Sun State Trailers can help you spec, finance, and service it locally.
What Is a Dry Freight Trailer?

Dry freight trailers are enclosed trailers designed to protect goods from weather, road debris, and theft. They're the industry standard for hauling general cargo and are used in nearly every sector, from retail distribution to e-commerce to regional delivery.

items.title: Enclosed, Weather-Proof Design
items.intro: Keeps cargo safe from rain, sun, wind, and road grime.

items.title: Standardized Sizing
items.intro: Most dry vans come in 28', 48', or 53' lengths, making them adaptable for various hauls.

items.title: Dock-Level Compatibility
items.intro: Built for fast, efficient loading and unloading at warehouses and retail locations.

items.title: Durable Construction
items.intro: Options for composite, aluminum, or galvanized steel exteriors to match load demands and environments.

props.text: Dry freight trailers are ideal for packaged goods, non-perishable food and beverages, building materials, textiles, electronics, and furniture; the possibilities are endless. If your cargo doesn't need refrigeration but still needs protection from the elements, this trailer type is likely your best option.
Why Dry Freight Trailers Make Business Sense
For many owner-operators, the dry van trailer is their most-used and most-profitable asset. Here's why.

items.text: Versatility means more load opportunities — dry vans can handle a wide range of freight types, giving you more freedom to accept backhauls, pivot with demand, or serve multiple clients with one piece of equipment
Easier to maintain — with no refrigeration unit or hydraulic systems, dry freight trailers are generally easier and cheaper to maintain, meaning fewer breakdowns and lower service costs
Maximized fuel efficiency — modern dry vans feature lightweight materials and aerodynamic designs, letting you haul more without exceeding DOT weight limits
Strong ROI — low maintenance needs, consistent demand, and better fuel economy make dry freight trailers one of the best investments in trucking

props.text: How to Choose the Right Dry Freight Trailer
The "right" trailer depends on your hauls, routes, and long-term business goals. Here are a few key points to keep in mind.

items.text: Consider size and payload — while 53-foot trailers are common for long-haul freight, a 48' or even 28' may be better suited for local or regional deliveries. Think about where you'll be hauling and how often you'll be loading and unloading.

Look at the wall and floor materials — do you need reinforced walls for heavy cargo? Will your trailer be exposed to moisture or corrosive environments? Composite and aluminum walls, high-tensile steel rear frames, and scuff-resistant floors can help extend the life of your trailer.

Don't forget your budget — Sun State Trailers offers trailer financing options to keep your cash flow stable while you invest in quality equipment. Whether you're buying new or considering an upgrade, we'll help you compare cost vs. value.
